tx-sos-2026-ballot-cert.title: Ballot Certification Report, 2026 November General Election (state and district offices)
tx-sos-2026-ballot-cert.note: Read county by county, all 254 counties, 1,396 pages (the cover and 1,395 report pages, every page stamp accounted for): offices, names and parties only. 490 state races kept (13,488 county lines of their candidates; every county's list of each race agreed). The list's order is kept as the ballot order. Left for the federal pages, or read into the local races (the next source): county court (257 county lists, 300 candidate lines); county office (1,575 county lists, 1,772 candidate lines); district attorney (56 county lists, 63 candidate lines); federal (563 county lists, 1,442 candidate lines); justice of the peace (749 county lists, 853 candidate lines). A race's county_ids are the counties whose lists carry it. Names are printed in capitals and shown in ordinary capitals (a sitting member as the roster spells the name).

tx-sos-2026-ballot-cert-local.title: Ballot Certification Report, 2026 November General Election (county and precinct offices, county courts and district attorneys)
tx-sos-2026-ballot-cert-local.note: The same report, read county by county for all 254 counties: under each county, every heading for a county or precinct office, a county court, a criminal district attorney or a district attorney, and the name and party lines under it; the report has no contact columns. 2,988 candidate lines under 2,637 printed contests gave 2,982 candidates in 2,631 contests (2 printed under more than one county, every copy agreeing). The state part of this loader counts the same headings and lines. Every one of these offices is elected on party lines. The report's order is kept as the ballot order where it is the order of the party columns (Election Code 52.091: Republican, Democratic, Libertarian, Green, then independents): 2,630 of 2,631 contests. The Secretary's cover certifies the state and district offices and does not say who certified the county and precinct names. Names are printed in capitals and shown in ordinary capitals.

tx-sos-2026-candidate-list.title: Candidate Information: candidates in the 2026 November General Election (the Secretary's candidate list, as its own page asks for it)
tx-sos-2026-candidate-list.note: One request, the one the page itself makes, answered with 3,967 rows (2,571,689 bytes; the SHA-256 is of the bytes as fetched). Kept: the 3,095 rows for county and precinct offices, county courts and district attorneys, cut down in memory to office type, office number, county, office title, the name as on the ballot (not kept for anyone the list no longer counts as a candidate), party, the two status codes and the kind of candidate. The mailing address, e-mail, website and occupation columns are never read; 0 kept cells looked like contact details and were blanked. A contest is the list's office number; a candidate counts when the list's status is Candidate in the General Election; party W is a declared write-in. Compared with the certification contest by contest: 2,628 read the same, 2 differ in a name, 1 filed under another precinct number, 0 not on the list at all; county by county, 251 of 254 counties read the same throughout. From the list alone: 82 declared write-in candidates, 14 contests where only a write-in declared, 1 with no candidate left. Left off: the 31 candidacies the list marks as ended (18 withdrawn, 8 deceased, 5 declared ineligible). Every kept row is accounted for: 2,982 printed candidates, 82 declared write-ins, 31 ended, 0 without a readable name, 0 in contests not loaded.

local_calendar.t: On November 3, 2026 Texas counties elect, on party lines, a county judge, the county commissioners for precincts 2 and 4, a district clerk and a county clerk, a county treasurer and a county surveyor where the county has one, the judges of the county courts at law and the justices of the peace. The Secretary of State's lists also carry a criminal district attorney in 47 counties, 19 county commissioners elected for the rest of a term, and 101 contests for a sheriff, tax assessor-collector, county attorney, constable or district attorney, 75 of them for the rest of a term. Cities, school districts and water, hospital and other local districts hold their own elections on a uniform date, the first Saturday in May or the November date, and the Secretary of State's calendar says many use May.

The Secretary's cover certifies the state and district offices and does not say who certified the county and precinct names printed in the same report, so a county's own sample ballot is the authority. gaps.w: city, school district and special district races
gaps.r: The Secretary of State's certification covers federal, state, district, county and precinct offices only. Cities, school districts and water, hospital and other districts that vote on November 3 publish their candidates county by county or one by one, with no statewide list, so none of them is here yet.

Counties of 75,000 people or more elect three directors of their appraisal district at the general election for state and county officers (Tax Code 6.0301). The candidates file with the county clerk or elections administrator, and no statewide list names them.

The certification and the candidate list name candidates, so a county or precinct office that drew no candidate and no declared write-in is in neither and is not shown. The county's own sample ballot is the place to check.
